modules.title: Name the whole
modules.skill: Identify the whole, then read a fraction as equal parts OF that whole.

items.title: A chocolate bar
items.story: A chocolate bar is split into 4 equal squares. Riya eats 1 square.

steps.prompt: What is the whole in this story?

choices.text: all 4 equal squares of the bar
choices.feedback: Yes - the whole is all 4 equal squares of the bar, all of it together.
That is the PART we are naming, not the whole it comes from.
That is a number from the story, but it is not the whole group.

steps.hint: The whole is all 4 equal squares of the bar - the full group before we pick any part.

steps.prompt: How many EQUAL parts is the whole cut into?

choices.feedback: Right - all 4 equal parts make the bottom number.
That is only the shaded parts. The bottom counts EVERY equal part.

choices.text: The parts are not equal, so we cannot say
choices.feedback: In this picture the parts ARE equal, so we can count them.

steps.hint: Count every equal part, shaded and not: there are 4.

steps.prompt: Which fraction names the shaded part?

choices.feedback: Yes - 1 shaded out of 4 equal parts is 1/4.
The top and bottom are swapped. Top is the shaded count, bottom is the total.
The bottom should be the TOTAL equal parts, not shaded added to total.

steps.hint: Top = shaded (1); bottom = all equal parts (4).

solution.text: The whole is all 4 equal squares of the bar.
It is cut into 4 equal parts, so the bottom number is 4.
1 of those parts are shaded, so the top number is 1.

items.check: Shaded 1/4 and the bottom 4 counts every equal part.
items.explain: Why must the parts be equal before we write a fraction?

modules.rule: A fraction a/b means the whole is cut into b EQUAL parts and we take a of them.
modules.transfer: Draw a bar, cut it into 6 equal parts, shade 5. Which fraction did you make?
teach: Always start by naming the whole: 'The whole is all 8 slices' or 'the whole is the chocolate bar'.
The bottom number (denominator) tells how many EQUAL parts the whole is cut into.
The top number (numerator) tells how many of those equal parts we are talking about.
contrast: If the parts are NOT equal, you cannot name a simple fraction yet.

modules.title: Part and the rest
modules.skill: Shaded + unshaded = the whole, so the two parts always add back to 1.

items.title: Coloured squares
items.story: A grid of 8 equal squares has 3 squares coloured. The rest are plain.

steps.prompt: What fraction is shaded (the part we are told about)?

choices.feedback: Yes - 3 of 8 equal parts are shaded, that is 3/8.
That is the leftover part, not the shaded part the story gives us.
The bottom must be ALL equal parts (8), not just the leftover ones.

steps.hint: Shaded parts over all parts: 3 out of 8.

steps.prompt: The whole is 1. How do we find the part that is NOT shaded?

choices.feedback: Yes - the leftover is the whole minus the shaded part.
Adding makes more than one whole. The rest is a PART of the same whole.
That repeats the shaded part. We want the part that is LEFT.

steps.hint: Take the whole and subtract the shaded part: 1 - shaded.

steps.prompt: So what fraction is plain (not coloured)?

choices.feedback: Yes - 5 of 8 parts are left, which is 5/8.
That is the SHADED amount. Re-read: we were asked for the part left over.
The bottom stays the total number of equal parts, not the shaded count.

steps.hint: 8 parts minus 3 shaded leaves 5 parts.

solution.text: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts.

items.check: Shaded 3/8 and leftover 5/8 add back to the whole, 1.
items.explain: Why do the shaded and leftover parts always share the same bottom number?

modules.title: Equivalent fractions
modules.skill: Multiply (or divide) the top AND bottom by the SAME number to rename a fraction.

items.title: Halves to quarters
items.story: A cake is cut in 2 equal halves, then every half is cut again into 2.

steps.prompt: We want to rewrite 1/2 with bottom 4. What do we do to the bottom?

choices.feedback: Yes - 2 x 2 = 4, so we scale by 2.
Adding changes the value. 2 + 2 is not a scaling of 2.
That would give 6, not 4. Check the target bottom.

steps.hint: 2 times what gives 4? That same move must happen to the top.

steps.prompt: To keep the SAME value, what must we do to the top?

choices.feedback: Yes - scale top and bottom by the same 2 to keep the value.
Adding the same number to top and bottom changes the fraction's value.

choices.text: Leave the top as it is
choices.feedback: Changing only the bottom makes a different fraction, not an equal one.

steps.hint: Whatever we do to the bottom, we do the SAME to the top.

steps.prompt: So 1/2 is equal to which fraction?

choices.feedback: Yes - 1 x 2 over 2 x 2 is 2/4, equal to 1/2.
This added 2 to both. Equivalent fractions come from multiplying, not adding.
Only the top was scaled. Both top and bottom must scale by the same number.

steps.hint: Top: 1 x 2 = 2. Bottom: 2 x 2 = 4.

solution.text: Multiply the top by the same 2: 1 x 2 = 2.

items.check: 2/4 scales back down by 2 to 1/2, so they are equal.
items.explain: Why does multiplying top and bottom by the same number keep the value?

items.title: Give away four-fifths
items.story: Dev has 40 marbles and gives 4/5 of them away.

steps.prompt: '4/5 of 40' - what does the word 'of' tell us to do?

choices.text: Multiply the fraction by the quantity
choices.feedback: Yes - a fraction OF an amount means we multiply.

choices.text: Add the fraction to the quantity
choices.feedback: 'of' is not adding - it takes a part of the amount.

choices.text: Subtract the top from the quantity
choices.feedback: 'of' is not subtracting - it shares the amount into equal parts.

steps.hint: 'of' means multiply the fraction by the quantity.

steps.prompt: First find ONE equal part: 40 divided into 5 parts is...?

choices.feedback: Yes - one part is 40 divided by 5 = 8.
That divided by the TOP (4). We divide by the bottom to make one equal part.
That is the whole amount, not one equal part of it.

steps.hint: Divide by the BOTTOM: 40 divided by 5.

steps.prompt: So how many marbles are LEFT (not given away)?

choices.feedback: Yes - left = 40 - 32 = 8.
That is the amount given AWAY - we were asked how many are LEFT.
That is the whole starting amount - some was given away, so less is left.

steps.hint: Given away is 4 x 8 = 32; the rest is left.

items.check: The answer 8 fits within the whole of 40 marbles.
